bremerton.label: Quarters Arcade
bremerton.observation: Opened with about 36 games in 2,000 square feet.
bremerton.interpretation: A dedicated all-ages arcade provides a public gathering point.

bremerton.label: Another Castle → Town Portal
bremerton.observation: The historical barcade opened in 2016. A 2024 local retrospective reports that the Another Castle operation was taken over and reopened as Town Portal.
bremerton.interpretation: This is a documented transition in name and operation, rather than evidence that barcade activity disappeared from the location.
bremerton.status: Another Castle brand replaced by Town Portal; current Town Portal website lists downtown Bremerton location

bremerton.label: Ashley’s Pub
bremerton.observation: A board-game pub opened and later developed a rotating pinball selection.
bremerton.interpretation: Board-game and pinball activity meet in one venue.

bremerton.label: Beyond Reality / VR arcade
bremerton.interpretation: The local scene diversifies into another technology and play format.

bremerton.label: Tik Tok’s Workshop
bremerton.observation: A pinball-focused venue opened, linked in the research to an existing collection and repair practice.
bremerton.interpretation: Technical and collecting activity becomes a permanent public venue.

bremerton.label: The Game Wizard / Blue Sky Hobbies
bremerton.observation: Contemporary 2015 reporting places this hobby and game shop across the street from Quarters Arcade.
bremerton.interpretation: A neighboring tabletop and hobby destination broadens what a visit to the arcade district can include.

bremerton.label: SEEfilm Cinema
bremerton.observation: The project author identifies SEEfilm as the nearby movie theater. Contemporary reporting describes cinema, hobby shopping and arcade play as a day of activities on Fourth Street.
bremerton.interpretation: Film-going is part of the surrounding entertainment ecosystem; no shared ownership or causal link is asserted.

bremerton.label: Roxy Theatre
bremerton.observation: The Roxy reopened following renovation in 2018; its current program includes cult, classic, documentary and other screenings.
bremerton.interpretation: Another cultural destination adds a different form of film-going to the neighborhood.

bremerton.label: Cafe Omni
bremerton.observation: Its current official website places Cafe Omni at 206 Burwell Street. The opening year has not been established here.
bremerton.interpretation: A cafe adds food, rest and informal gathering to the wider scene. It is separate from the unconfirmed upstairs bookshop.

bremerton.label: Upstairs bookshop
bremerton.observation: I recall a bookshop above the barcade/hobby corner. Its name, exact location and historical dates still need confirmation.
bremerton.interpretation: Included as a firsthand research lead rather than an identified, dated business.
